That skillet chicken you’re already making is a perfect foundation, so here’s a small upgrade that stays very close to what you’re doing:

Take your chicken breast, salt and pepper it like usual. Heat your cast iron skillet with a bit of oil, medium heat. Cook the chicken until browned on both sides and just about done, then take it out and set it aside.

Now, in that same pan (don’t clean it), toss in a bit of chopped onion. Let it cook for a few minutes until it softens. Add a clove or two of garlic if you have it. Then pour in about half a cup of chicken broth and squeeze in some lemon juice (even bottled is fine). Scrape the bottom of the pan with your spoon—that’s where the flavor is.

Let that simmer for a couple of minutes, then put the chicken back in and let it finish cooking in the liquid for another few minutes. The sauce will reduce a bit and coat the chicken.

That’s it. Same core method you already know, just one extra step that turns it into something that feels more like a “meal” than a piece of meat on a plate.

If you want to keep building from there over time, you can swap the lemon for mushrooms, or add a spoonful of mustard, or a splash of cream—but no rush. Just one variation at a time keeps it enjoyable.
